co_pink_floyd_area.blurb: The Pink Floyd Area is a bouldering-only zone on the far western edge of the Mecca Boulder Area, in Unaweep Canyon on Nine Mile Hill near Grand Junction. It is a dense scatter of boulders, with many separate blocks each holding a handful of problems; Main Boulder, Barn Block, Megalomania Block and Coy Rock are among the larger ones. The style leans vertical, with plenty of slab and some slightly overhanging lines. Most problems fall between V0 and V4, with a thinner tail of harder ones reaching V10. It feels secluded and away from the highway, and the canyon wall casts shade over it in the late afternoon. Climbers rate it as the best concentration on Nine Mile Hill for quantity, density and quality.

wa_bouldering_in_tumwater_canyon.blurb: Tumwater Canyon holds a run of granite boulders along Highway 2 just west of Leavenworth, in the eastern Cascades. Every problem here is bouldering, with a wide spread of difficulty: plenty of V0 to V4, a healthy middle, and a tail reaching into the V10s and beyond. The biggest clusters are Swiftwater Boulders and the Beach and Forest Area, followed by Pitless Avocado and the Labyrinth. Swiftwater is fine-grained granite with a few schist blocks mixed in. Approaches are short and it is a quick drive from town. Bouldering around Leavenworth is described as best in spring and summer, though the area can be climbed through the year, with occasional snow in winter.

ca_mission_gorge.blurb: Mission Gorge is a long-established crag inside Mission Trails Regional Park in San Diego County, a short drive off I-8. Trad is the largest share, with sport, top-rope and a little bouldering rounding it out. Grades begin around 5.4 and reach 5.12, with most routes between 5.7 and 5.10 and a smaller group of harder lines. The main concentrations are Middle Earth, the Main Wall and the Limbo Area, followed by Lunch Rock and a separate bouldering section. The Main Wall mixes cracks, chimneys, bolted lines and some aid. The gorge sits low, at only a few hundred feet above sea level.

_expect.name: New Durham Area (Longstack, Devil's Den, Rines Hill, etc.)

nh_new_durham_area_longstack_devil_s_den.blurb: These crags lie on the east side of Lake Winnipesaukee, where the towns of New Durham, Alton and Wolfeboro meet, and several offer views over the lake. Trad is the main event, with a smaller helping of bouldering and sport, plus a few top-ropes. Grades run from about 5.4 to 5.13, with most routes between 5.7 and 5.10. Longstack Precipice is the largest crag and dries quickly, often climbable within a couple of hours after rain. Devil's Den has four main cliff areas between 40 and 75 feet tall, and its slabs freeze into ice climbs in winter. Rines Hill is mainly bouldering, and Mt. Molly and Rand Mountain add smaller crags. Ice and mixed lines also form at Mount Molly and Pleasant Valley.

ny_near_trapps_the.blurb: The Near Trapps is one of the main cliffs of the Gunks, on the Shawangunk ridge near New Paltz, a long escarpment of nearly white quartz conglomerate. The cliff runs from about 30 to 200 feet high and is overwhelmingly trad, with a sizable bouldering section at its base. Grades run from 5.4 up to 5.12, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.11. Climbs follow corners, cracks, aretes and slabs, descents are easy, and many routes have rappel anchors. The north end is the most popular and densely packed, the middle has some loose rock, and the far south end holds good climbs but needs a longer walk. Workout Wall is one of the bigger named sections.

wa_exit_34_middle_fork_amp_taylor_river.blurb: This area covers the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley north of I-90 near North Bend, in the Central-West Cascades, with much of it inside the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. The rock is solid gray granite, often in slabby buttresses scattered along the valley. Sport routes are the largest share, with bouldering and trad close behind and a few alpine lines. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.14, mostly 5.8 to 5.12, and the boulders go up to the V9 range. Bessemer Mountain holds a cluster of sport routes, mostly 5.12 and around it. Stegosaurus Butte, Middle Fork Bouldering and the Fee Demo Wall are other large sectors, and Mount Garfield has committing alpine routes. Much of the valley remains undeveloped.
